title: Oklahoma's 1985 National Title: 25-10 Orange Bowl Win Over Penn State
question: How did Oklahoma win the 1985 national championship?
answer: Oklahoma beat No. 1 Penn State 25-10 in the Orange Bowl on Jan. 1, 1986. With Miami losing to Tennessee in the Sugar Bowl the same day, the Sooners finished No. 1 for Barry Switzer's third national title.
summary: Oklahoma beat No. 1 Penn State 25-10 in the Jan. 1, 1986 Orange Bowl to claim the 1985 national title behind freshman QB Jamelle Holieway and Keith Jackson.
body: The 1985 title run nearly fell apart in October. Miami beat Oklahoma 27-14 in Norman on Oct. 19, and starting quarterback Troy Aikman broke his ankle in that game. Barry Switzer turned the wishbone over to true freshman Jamelle Holieway, who ended up leading the team in rushing with 861 yards.

The defense carried a lot of weight too. Linebacker Brian Bosworth won the first Butkus Award, and nose guard Tony Casillas took home the Lombardi Award. Oklahoma ran the table in the Big Eight and earned a trip to Miami to face unbeaten, top-ranked Penn State.

Penn State scored first, but Oklahoma took over in the second quarter. Holieway hit sophomore tight end Keith Jackson on a 71-yard touchdown pass, and kicker Tim Lashar added field goals from 26, 31 and 21 yards before halftime. Lashar kicked a fourth field goal in the third quarter, and Lydell Carr sealed the game with a 61-yard touchdown run in the fourth. Oklahoma's defense forced five turnovers, and Lashar and defensive back Sonny Brown shared the game's MVP honors.

Oklahoma still needed help, and it came in New Orleans, where Tennessee beat Miami 35-7 in the Sugar Bowl. The Sooners finished 11-1 and No. 1 in both the AP and coaches polls. It was the program's sixth national championship and Switzer's third.
